learning: Iteration 9 gave the best slalom progress so far (0.68) with 2/20 finishes. Narrower track (iteration 8) and higher turn authority did not help. Yaw inertia is the lever under test.
notes: Runnable package: the Builder's 0.45 kg mass proposal on the iteration 9 controller, with no gain changes. Only mass differs from the raced design, so the race isolates yaw inertia on the slalom.
rationale: The Builder's proposal keeps the iteration 9 design (mass 0.5 kg, body_length 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, 7 sensors at +/-0.036 m, 0.012 m pitch, 12 mm footprints, lead 0.06 m) and changes only mass to 0.45 kg. Iteration 9 is the best measured design (741.9). Its oval held 20/20 at 1.92 s, its s-bend held 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.295, and its slalom reached progress 0.68 with 2/20 finishes and line_loss_events 1.15. Across iterations 7 to 9, lower yaw inertia was the only change that raised slalom progress. Iteration 8 showed that narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m adds s-bend jitter (0.342) and cuts slalom progress, so the track stays at 0.10 m. The controller that raced in iteration 9 (kp 3.6, kd 0.9, ki 0, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, linear weights -2 to +2) is kept unchanged, so the mass change is the only variable under test. Expected: slalom progress above 0.68 with line_loss_events trending toward 1.0, the oval at 20/20, and the s-bend at 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation under 0.35. Fallback: if s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses trials, or the score falls below 741.9, return to mass 0.5 kg. The measurements cover slalom and s-bend jitter, completion time and line loss so the next iteration can judge the result.
